senses.gloss: m.anthropeus (man), an assumed form for ἄνθρωπος, for the purpose of deriving another assumed form (אַנְתְּרוֹפִּיָּא) anthropeia (woman).
units: Gen. R. s. 18; s. 31 did you ever hear people say gynios and gyneia (from γύνη, woman), or anthropeus, anthropeia, gabra (man) gabratha (woman)? but you do say (in Hebrew) ish and ish-sha, both of the same root (as an evidence of the primitiveness of the Hebrew language).
